quotes.verbatim_quote:
an event can be diatonically
transposed to create 6 other
events, but some of them will
be intervallically identical.
quotes.why_load_bearing: States a key structural property: diatonic transposition yields 6 other events, but intervallic identity collapses some of those.

quotes.topic: Diatonic transposition of episodes and modal correspondence
quotes.verbatim_quote:
an episode can be diatonically
transposed to create 6 other
episodes, where each corresponds
to a different mode.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Establishes the one-to-one link between each transposed episode and one of the seven modes.

quotes.topic: Melodic/contrapuntal/harmonic scope of events and episodes
quotes.verbatim_quote: Both events and episodes can be melodic, contrapuntal, harmonic or in any combination...
quotes.why_load_bearing: Broadens the application of these terms beyond melody to counterpoint and harmony.

quotes.topic: Naming rationale for sus4 chord nomenclature
quotes.verbatim_quote: My suggestion for a suitable name for this chord would be: G [sus4].
quotes.why_load_bearing: Justifies the author's preferred chord-naming system (sus4 over C2) on grounds of musician legibility.

quotes.verbatim_quote: Of course, this applies to all of the inversions as well...
quotes.why_load_bearing: Extends the sus4 chord names explicitly to all inversions.
